verdict.justification: Deliverable B demonstrates far superior strategic thinking and mathematical utilization of the prompt's constraints. Crucially, B recognizes that because LPI has a capacity of 1,500–2,500 units/month against a monthly demand of only 800 sets, LiIon does not need LPI to remain on the hook for the full 6-month transition period; instead, B proposes a compressed Last-Time Build (LTB) where LPI ramps to 2,500/month and finishes the required ~5,200 bridge sets by Week 10 (only ~7 weeks past their desired exit date). In contrast, Deliverable A asks LPI to keep supplying month-by-month through May/June 2027, which is a much harder sell to a hostile supplier demanding an immediate exit. B also integrates the tooling transfer math much better, showing how an early plastics "mould-out" in W1–W3 allows tooling release by W4–W6 so that the ~25-day transit plus 3–4 months of plastics work finishes ahead of the 4–5 month electronics critical path. Furthermore, B provides a much sharper, multi-variable ZOPA table and examines both LiIon's and LPI's BATNAs. My only minor criticism of B is a stray meta-comment in Section 9 referring to "the assignment brief" and "workspace and attachment folders", whereas A stays strictly in-character, but B's analytical and operational depth makes it the clear winner.

decisive_issues.issue: Fails to leverage LPI's 1,500-2,500/month excess capacity to compress the exit timeline, instead asking a hostile supplier to stay on through May/June 2027.
